title: Copper Supply Outlook to 2035: The Permitting and Capital Cost Cliff
key_claim: Average copper-mine permitting time globally has risen from 11 years (2010-15) to 18 years (2020-25); capital cost per tonne of new capacity up 86% in real terms over the same period.
notes: Anchor for the lead-time and capex compression claim.

title: Energy Transition Metals 2026: Copper as the Binding Constraint
key_claim: Energy-transition copper demand to triple by 2035 vs 2024 baseline; data-centre and AI infrastructure now contribute 18% of incremental demand growth, up from 4% in 2022.
notes: Anchor for AI-and-data-centre demand surge claim.

title: Critical Minerals Tracker — Q1 2026
key_claim: Recycled copper supply meeting 32% of demand in 2025, projected to reach only 38% by 2030 even under aggressive circular-economy scenarios; primary-mine output remains the binding constraint.
notes: Anchor for the recycling-cannot-close-gap claim — important counter to circular-economy optimism.

title: Major copper miners cut 2030 production guidance amid permitting delays
key_claim: BHP, Rio Tinto, Freeport-McMoRan, Anglo American, and Codelco have collectively cut 2030 production guidance by 1.4 Mt year-on-year; CEO commentary cites permitting and water-licence constraints as primary drivers.
notes: Landed-on-the-ground signal for the corporate-guidance reset.
